job.title: Junior School Specialist Teacher - Art
job.description:
About Us:
Nestled within the picturesque landscapes of the Mornington Peninsula, Toorak College empowers our students through academic and personal growth so they will thrive in their future. With a legacy spanning 150 years, we remain committed to igniting curiosity and empowering students to shine in the world beyond our gates. With state-of-the-art facilities and a close-knit community, Toorak College provides an ideal environment for both students and staff to thrive.
  
Our Junior School provides a rich and engaging learning environment where students are encouraged to explore their interests, develop confidence and discover their individual strengths. Our specialist programs provide opportunities for students to extend their learning beyond the classroom and develop skills that inspire creativity, curiosity and a lifelong love of learning.

Role & Responsibilities:
As a part-time Junior School Specialist Teacher in Art at Toorak College, you will demonstrate:  
  • A strong commitment to excellence in education, with experience, flair and passion for Art;
  • A proven capacity for innovative, creative and engaging teaching practice;
  • The ability to develop inspiring Art learning experiences that encourage students to explore, experiment and express themselves;
  • An ability to differentiate learning to meet the diverse needs, abilities and interests of students;
  • A commitment to fostering creativity, confidence, curiosity and a positive approach to learning; and
  • A desire to work collaboratively within a high-performing and collegial teaching team.
The focus of this position is the teaching of Art across the Junior School (P–6), at 0.74 FTE. The teaching allocation will be determined according to the successful candidate’s expertise, experience and the College’s operational requirements. The position is worked Monday and Wednesday to Friday, with Tuesdays not required.

About You:
You are passionate about Art and enjoy inspiring young students to explore their creativity and develop confidence in their own ideas and abilities. You will bring enthusiasm, strong subject knowledge and an engaging approach to the classroom, creating a positive environment where students feel encouraged to take creative risks, experiment and express themselves. You will be an educator who understands the important role the Arts play in developing well-rounded, confident and curious young people and who is committed to providing meaningful and engaging learning experiences for every student.

Qualifications & Requirements:
  • Degree qualified in Primary Education, with relevant qualification in Art education.
  • Current Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) registration is essential.
  • Demonstrated experience for teaching Art within a Primary School setting.
  • Excellent communication skills and strong ability to connect with and motivate students.
  • A proven capacity for innovative, flexible and research-based teaching practice.
  • A commitment to collaborative practice and ongoing professional learning.
Why Choose Toorak College?
  • Beautiful Mornington Peninsula location – work within your community.
  • Toorak College staff have access to our onsite Athletics and Gym facilities.
  • On-site café and regular catered Morning Teas and Lunches for staff.
  • Toorak College prides itself on a supportive and collegial culture among staff and students.
  • Utilise cutting-edge facilities and resources.
  • Access to our outstanding Employee Assistance Program.
Application Process:
If you’re ready to join our teaching team, we want to hear from you!  Please submit a 2-page resume, cover letter, and the name and the contact details of two confidential referees.  Your application should be addressed to Mrs Kristy Kendall, School Principal, Toorak College.
  
You can find out more about us at www.careers.toorakcollege.vic.edu.au
  
Please note: You must have full working rights to work in Australia, and a current Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) Registration to apply.

The closing date for applications is 9am Monday 7th September 2026.

We would like to inform potential applicants that the role may close earlier if we receive a high volume of suitable candidates. We encourage candidates to submit applications early, as interviews may commence prior to the closing date. Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
  
Toorak College is committed to a Child Safe school environment, and we have extensive recruitment and screening processes in place. All interested applicants are encouraged to read and familiarise themselves with Toorak Colleges' Child Safety and Wellbeing Policy located on the Toorak College website.
  
Toorak College is a child safe organisation which welcomes all children, young people and their families. Toorak College is committed to the safety and wellbeing of all children, including those under the care and supervision of the School. The School recognises the importance of, and its responsibility for, ensuring a safe and supportive environment which respects the rights of children and fosters their enrichment and wellbeing.
  
Toorak College is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to establishing a welcoming and inclusive environment for all members of the School Community.

job.title: Junior School Teacher - Full Time
job.description:
About Us:
Nestled within the picturesque landscapes of the Mornington Peninsula, Toorak Colleges’ reputation in innovation and limitless possibilities is what sees it continue to be a choice destination for educators.  With a legacy spanning 150 years, we remain committed to igniting curiosity and empowering students to thrive in the modern world.  With beautiful grounds and a connected community, Toorak College provides an ideal environment for both students, educators and operational staff to work together to bring about the change we wish to see in the world tomorrow.
  
At Toorak College, our Junior School is guided by the principles of the Reggio Emilia educational philosophy, where curiosity, creativity and inquiry are at the heart of every student’s learning journey.  We believe that children are capable, confident learners, and we create rich learning environments that encourage exploration, collaboration and meaningful connections with the world around them.

Role & Responsibilities:
As a Junior School teacher at Toorak College, you will:  
  • Plan, deliver and evaluate engaging, differentiated learning experiences that meet the diverse academic, social and emotional needs of students.
  • Create a positive, inclusive and stimulating classroom environment that fosters curiosity, creativity, independence and a lifelong love of learning through inquiry-based practices.
  • Use assessment data and evidence-informed teaching strategies to monitor student progress, provide meaningful feedback and support continuous improvement.
  • Build strong partnerships with students, families and colleagues, contributing to a collaborative and connected Junior School community.
  • Contribute to the development and delivery of innovative curriculum and learning experiences aligned with the Schools’ educational philosophy and strategic priorities.
  • Support the wellbeing, personal growth and holistic development of every student while maintaining a safe and nurturing learning environment.
  • Actively contribute to the broader life of the School through co-curricular programs, professional learning and community events.
This position is offered on a full-time basis, with flexibility for the successful candidate to be considered for either ongoing or fixed-term employment, depending on their suitability and the College’s operational requirements.  Specific classes and year levels taught will be determined according to the candidate’s expertise, experience, and operational requirements.

About You:
You are an enthusiastic and dedicated educator who believes in creating meaningful learning experiences that inspire curiosity, confidence and a genuine love of learning. You enjoy working collaboratively with colleagues and value the strong partnerships that can be built with students and their families to support each child's growth and development.  With a contemporary approach to teaching and learning, you embrace inquiry-based practice and appreciate the principles of the Reggio Emilia philosophy, creating engaging learning environments where students feel supported, challenged and empowered to achieve their personal best.
  
Above all, you are committed to fostering student wellbeing, demonstrating professional excellence and contributing positively to the vibrant life of the Toorak College community.
  
Qualifications & Requirements:
  • Degree qualified in Primary Education or equivalent.
  • Current VIT registration essential.
  • Demonstrated experience and passion for teaching in a Junior School setting.
  • Excellent communication skills and strong ability to connect with and motivate students.
  • A proven capacity for innovative, flexible and research-based teaching practice.
Why Choose Toorak College?
  • Beautiful Mornington Peninsula location – a walk from the beach.
  • Toorak College staff have access to our onsite Athletics and Gym facilities.
  • On-site café and regularly catered Morning Teas and Lunches for staff.
  • Toorak College prides itself on a supportive and collegial culture among staff and students.
  • Utilise cutting-edge facilities and resources.
  • Access to our outstanding Employee Assistance Program.
Application Process:
Please submit a two (2) page resume, covering letter, including the name and contact details of two confidential referees.  Your application should be addressed to Mrs Kristy Kendall, School Principal, Toorak College.

You can find out more about us at www.careers.toorakcollege.vic.edu.au

Please note: You must have full working rights to work in AUS to apply for this position and hold a current Victorian Institute of Teaching (VIT) Registration.

The closing date for applications is 9am Monday 7th September 2026.

 We would like to inform potential applicants that the role may close earlier if we receive a high volume of suitable candidates.  We encourage candidates to submit applications early, as interviews may commence prior to the closing date.  Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted at the time of shortlisting, all applications will be acknowledged at the conclusion of the process.
  
Toorak College is committed to a Child Safe school environment, and we have extensive recruitment and screening processes in place. All interested applicants are encouraged to read and familiarise themselves with Toorak Colleges' Child Safety and Wellbeing Policy located on the Toorak College website.
